The First Chapter.
The Illustrious Goddess said: "O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Lord! Please tell me now!"
Then, one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), the purification of the body (dehaśuddhi), and thereafter the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma). || 1 ||
O Lord, wielder of the trident, bearer of the Pināka bow, O Mahādeva, let the mantra and the yantra be told in due order, by which one may attain purification upon this earth.
The illustrious Lord said: O lady of excellent hips, O you with eyes like a wagtail, O you of pure smiles, I shall speak;
I will proclaim the three principles, which are great, more secret than the secret.

O Goddess! O Beloved! For one who recites the Vidyā for the sake of supernatural powers (siddhi) without the three principles (tattvas), there shall be a loss of all goals and the recitation shall be fruitless.

O Great Goddess! One should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), the placement (nyāsa) which is most difficult to obtain, and then the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma); this is remembered as the triad of principles (tattvatraya). || 5 ||
O Maheśānī! One should perform everything conjoined with the letters of the Mātṛkā;
[one should contemplate] the Mātṛkā in the form of its letters, beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa'.
Having performed the Vedic and Tantric ablutions, one should perform the twilight prayers (sandhyā),
O Goddess of the lords of gods, having come into the vicinity of the sacrificial mandala.
Then, having performed the internal bath (antaḥsnāna), one should resort to the internal twilight devotion (antarsandhyā).
O beloved! I shall describe both the internal bath and the internal twilight devotion; listen.
First, one should perform meditation on the Guru, and thereafter perform the ritual bath;
O Maheśānī of pure smiles, having retained the life-force with the Praṇava! (9)
Drawing [the breath] up from the *mūlādhāra*, the wise one should lead it to the twelve-syllable [mantra];
he should then bathe in the pure sacred ford (*tīrtha*) at Puṣkara, which is endowed with the heart [of the mantra]. (10)
O Maheśānī, one should bring [the breath] from the *mūlādhāra* to the twelve-petaled lotus;
having established union with the Supreme Śiva, bliss arises. (11)
With that bliss, O Goddess of gods, one should bathe the living soul in the Anāhata [cakra];
thereafter, O Supreme Sovereign, one should contemplate the Ajapā, whose form is the vital breath.
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, O Pārvatī, one becomes purified by the bath!
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, perform the internal twilight rite (antaḥsandhyā) with diligence. 13.
At whatever time the union of Śiva and Śakti occurs, that is the twilight for the practitioners of Kula; one who is established in samādhi perceives it thus.
"In this way, O Great Goddess! one will certainly become purified by the twilight prayers (sandhyā).
The Śrī Devī said: O Supreme Lord! O Treasure of Compassion! please tell me about the Ajapā [mantra]. (15)
The illustrious Lord said: Listen, O Goddess of the gods! O beloved, I shall tell you that which is more secret than the secret;
I shall describe her meditation, by meditating upon which a person should perform the recitation. (16)

"Having performed meditation, O Great Goddess, one should begin the recitation [of the mantra], meditating thus: 'The Swan, who is eternal, infinite, and possessed of inexhaustible qualities, having naturally emerged and departing toward its own abode, resplendent like ten million suns, is the enchantress of the world. *Note: The term "haṃsa" here refers to the supreme consciousness or the *kuṇḍalinī-śakti*, visualized as departing from the heart-center toward the crown of the head.*
Having placed the six chakras in the center, one should contemplate the Ajapā, the supreme syllable.
Having extracted the seed-syllable of Śiva, place the seed-syllable of Bhṛgu after it;
then, O beautiful one, diligently join it with the half-moon and the Bindu. 18.
O lady of excellent hips! This knowledge is praised among the four castes;
O Goddess, without the recitation of this, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) is fruitless. (19)
Therefore, at the outset, one should mutter the Ajapā-vidyā, which is the form of the vital breath;
having muttered it one hundred and eight times, one should perform the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
O Pārvatī, O Goddess of the gods, having deposited the life-force (jīva) into all those syllables situated upon the petals of the six cakras, O Pārvatī! (21)
O Great Goddess, we diligently practice the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi). O Maheśānī of pure smiles, from the Mūlādhāra is the root-lotus! (22)
O Supreme Goddess! the root-portion, which possesses four petals and is endowed with ten syllables, is red in color and should always be cultivated by yogis. (23)
One should contemplate a beautiful, pure triangle with the seed-syllable of Earth (laṃ) situated in its center;
in the middle of that, one should meditate upon the god Śiva, who is dark and beautiful.
O Goddess, O Great Mistress! Here, Kuṇḍalinī, who is the supreme form of Prakṛti, always remains there, enveloping Śiva. (25)
The goddess Kuṇḍalī, whose form is that of a sleeping serpent, who resembles ten million flashes of lightning, who is praised by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and who is the very embodiment of Brahman.
O Goddess, having fixed the mind upon the mūlādhāra, one should always meditate on the four-petalled syllable, which is a means of crossing over and the destroyer of obstacles. (27)
Having joined it with the Bindu and the Half-moon (ardhacandra), one should then recite it ten times;
O Maheśānī! place that which belongs to the Ajapās upon the four petals.
Then, O Great Goddess, having led [the breath] together with the flower-swans to the Svādhiṣṭhāna, one should lead it to that city which is completely filled with water. (29)
O Supreme Goddess, just as the Mūlādhāra is graced by the earth, O Goddess of pure smiles, the Svādhiṣṭhāna is graced by water. (30)
It has lightning as its support for its six limbs, is endowed with the six syllables, joined with the letters va, bha, ma, ya, ra, and la, and is like a kunda flower. || 31 ||
O Goddess, having raised from the *mūlādhāra* the Kuṇḍalinī, whose form is Brahman, one should contemplate Śiva, the omniscient, residing in the *svādhiṣṭhāna*. (32)

O Goddess! Having led [the soul] to Maṇipura, one should perform the recitation (japa) of that [syllable]; having joined it with the Bindu and the Half-moon (ardhacandra), one should worship Śiva, who is thus adorned. || 33 ||
In that very place, O Supreme Goddess! perform the recitation of the six-syllabled mantra. O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign! it destroys the sixfold sins at that very moment.
O Goddess, the anus is four finger-breadths wide and possesses six petals and six qualities.
Thus ends the first chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī. || 1 ||
Now begins the second chapter:
Then, O Supreme Goddess! having led the vital air there by means of the mind, O Parameśvarī, the Maṇipūra is pierced. (1)
O Supreme Goddess! One should join the apāna with the samāna;
then, having pierced the river of Brahmā, the vital air (vāyu) went to Maṇipura.
The Śiva-liṅga situated there resembles a dark blue cloud;
its vessel is black in color, imperishable, and of a black form.
O Maheśānī! situated within that [cakra] is Mahādeva, the cause of all gods and others, known as Maṇipūra, possessing the luster of a great emerald. || 4 ||
O Goddess of the gods! Having meditated upon Śiva, one should mutter the ten-syllabled mantra;
make it begin with the letter *ḍa* and end with the letter *ka*, joined with the nasal dot (*bindu*) and the half-moon (*ardha*).
One should recite the syllable situated on the ten petals in order from the east and so forth;
the ten-petaled [lotus] is black in color, and the syllable has a black form.
O Goddess, by the recitation of the ten-syllable mantra, one destroys the sins of ten births; [it reveals] Mahādeva, who resides within that [lotus], the cause of all the gods and others.
Then, O Maheśānī, the vital air (vāyu) went to the city of Anāhata,
which is joined with twelve petals and endowed with twelve phonemes.
O Supreme Goddess! That leaf is white in color, and it is adorned with the letters from 'ka' to 'ṭha', the supreme syllable. (9)
O Supreme Goddess, the heart-lotus is always composed of pure sattva;
it has the form of a lamp-flame, and in its center is that which has the nature of Brahman.
O Dear One! Enveloped by twelve syllables and consisting of all powers, O Goddess of Gods, the life-force (jīva) always resides in front of it.
There, O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, the individual soul (jīva) always resides;
having perceived the vital breath (vāyu) joined with light as the soul, effect the dissolution of the mind.
The form of the self is the form of wind—always effortless, stainless, possessing the eight seed-syllables of the letter *ya*, and eternally radiant like gold. (13)
In that regard, O Goddess, make the syllable of the Sun (Āditya) joined with half of the Bindu;
having performed the recitation, O Maheśānī, perform it with effort, O beautiful one! 14.
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, whatever sin has been accumulated through twelve births, that is all surely destroyed at that very moment. 15.
For in this way, having pierced through, one returns to the pure [state], which is stainless, immaculate, pure, and endowed with the sixteen vowels. (16)
O Maheśānī! It is smoke-colored, called Viśuddha, and captivating;
O Goddess, situated in its center is the Ākāśa, whose form is Śakti.
One should gradually draw the individual soul (jīva) up by means of the Kuṇḍalinī and the Praṇava;
O Great Goddess, the mind is always the charioteer there in every respect. (18)
O Dear One! O Goddess! one should mentally perform everything beginning with the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and so forth;
and you should join the sixteenth vowel, O Goddess, together with the bindu and the half-moon (ardhacandra).
Then, O Supreme Goddess! one should mutter the sixteen-syllable mantra;
O Beloved, O Goddess, one should recite it ten times according to the sequence starting from the east.
O Goddess, whatever sin—whether auspicious or inauspicious—has been committed through sixteen lifetimes, that [sin] he would burn away by recitation, just as fire burns straw. 21.
Then, O Maheśānī! one should quickly lead the wind to the city of Ājñā;
that city, O Parameśānī, consists of two petals and four syllables. (22)

O Goddess! Having joined the letter with the nasal dot (bindu) and the half-moon (ardhacandra), which has the luster of gold and is always like the light of the moon, the practitioner should perform the recitation. || 23 ||
O Goddess! O Beloved! With the mind as charioteer, one should quickly lead the living soul, Kuṇḍalinī, to the city of Ājñā, wherein the mind contemplates within the mind.
O Supreme Sovereign! The mind always resides in Ājñāpura;
because it upholds the command of the Guru, this is remembered as Ājñāpura. (25)

O Supreme Goddess! Having thus pierced through the lattice-window of the gateway to the city of Sadāśiva, [one pierces] Kuṇḍalinī together with the individual soul (jīva) within the phenomenal world (prapañca).
O Goddess, with the mind as the charioteer, one should lead [the soul] to the city of Sadāśiva;
it is joined with the five vital breaths and endowed with the twenty-four [principles].
One should lead the eleven sense organs, the five great elements, and the intellect, ego, and mind toward the city of Śiva. (28)
"Then, having led [her] to the thousand-spoked [lotus], one should always unite her there with the mind.
Śrī Devī said:
"O Maheśāna, O Lord, having gone there, what did Kuṇḍalī do? (29)
The illustrious Lord said:
O beautiful one, O Goddess, when oneness arises through the twenty-four principles, the five vital breaths, the senses, and the imperishable [syllables], [then that state is attained]. (30)
There, O Goddess Maheśānī, one should contemplate the supreme Kuṇḍalī, who is intent upon the state of being,
by means of the path of meditation previously described.
O Goddess! It is the union of all souls and the upholder of all vidyās. || 31 ||
Thus ends the second chapter in the *Śrībhūtaśuddhitantra*, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī. || 2 ||
Now begins the third chapter.
The venerable Lord said: Listen, O Pārvatī! I shall declare a most wonderful secret.
O Goddess, it is more secret than the secret, to be well-guarded within the three worlds. || 1 ||
In the thousand-petaled lotus at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), where the god Sadāśiva resides, O Supreme Goddess!
there dwells the supreme goddess, having completely enveloped him. || 2 ||
One should join the Kuṇḍalinī there; then unity arises.
One should employ all the seed-syllables, from the letter 'a' to the letter 'kṣa', within that [seed]. || 3 ||
O Goddess of gods! O fair-faced one! Having first recited the Prāṇavidyā ten times in the mind, O Goddess, one should proceed to the supreme Kuṇḍalinī.
O Goddess, [it is] the city consisting of power, eternally composed of perpetual bliss;
O Beloved, it is the lotus endowed with a thousand petals, the eternal scripture.
O Maheśānī! O beloved! Within the center of the lotus is the city consisting of Śakti, where Sadāśiva resides, O Maheśānī! O Parameśvarī!
O Maheśānī! having reached Śiva—the deity who is pure reality and the like, stainless, and eternally immovable—Kuṇḍalī remains in the presence of Śiva.
O beloved, Kuṇḍalī indeed kisses the lotus-face of Śiva;
by applying the *sampuṭa* everywhere, she deludes the supreme Śiva.
O beloved, there Śiva, as Sadāśiva, becomes tranquil;
the Lord stands in the center of the lotus, free from desire and appearing like a corpse.
Mahādeva, in the form of Śava, is never [perceived as] a heart-pleasing being;
he is called the performer of action merely through conjunction with Śakti. (10)
Therefore, O Supreme Goddess, the preeminence of Śakti is proclaimed;
without Śakti, O Great Goddess, nothing at all exists. (11)
O beloved, Sadāśiva is the great preta; he alone is the certainty.
O Goddess, the city of Sadāśiva is Vaikuṇṭha, the supreme abode.
Having gone to the city of Sadāśiva, O beloved, the supreme goddess Kuṇḍalinī shall sport for a mere moment together with Sadāśiva.
O Goddess of gods, O beloved, union with Sadāśiva occurs;
at that very moment, O Supreme Goddess, nectar is produced.
With that nectar, O Goddess of gods, one should flood the six cakras in succession.
The illustrious Lord said:
Listen, O Pārvatī! I shall declare a secret that is difficult to find on earth—a mystery more secret than the secret, delightful, and rare throughout the three worlds. (15)

O Goddess of the Gods! having made the downward-breath (apāna) ascend and having filled the divine objective with the mantra of the vital breath (prāṇa), one should [awaken] the supreme power Kuṇḍalinī.
Having sequentially pierced through the cakras from the heart, which is charming to the individual soul (jīvātman),
one should unite it with the Supreme Brahman in the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown of the head.
Intellect, ego, and mind are the principles (tattvas), and primordial nature (prakṛti) is their body;
therefore, one should contemplate all these principles as being in the form of a seed.
Then, one should contemplate within the empty body, in the left side of the belly,
a cruel man consisting of all evil, with tawny hair.
Then, having visualized the smoky-colored seed-syllable of air at the navel, one should mutter it;
by expelling the air ten times, one should purify the body of sin. (20)
Then the practitioner of mantra should visualize the seed-syllable of fire (raṃ), red in color, within the heart of that evil one; by reciting it ten times, he becomes like the consuming fire.
O beloved, having generated that [fire], one burns this sinful body;
by meditating on the pure Varuṇa seed-syllable on the forehead and by reciting it, [the body is purified].
O lady of pure smiles, having produced the tenfold nectar-essence,
he was then born with a divine body, completely freed from all suffering.
Therefore, being intent upon it with such a disposition, one should wash away sin;
having understood the seed-syllable of the Earth (laṃ), one should contemplate it in the mūlādhāra.
O Goddess! O beautiful one! By reciting that [mantra] ten times, having produced the earth, [one produces] all the seeds and the principles (tattvas), O lady of pure smiles. (25)

O lady of pure smiles, O Supreme Goddess! one should deposit the seed-syllable in its proper place, starting from the Ājñā-cakra and ending with the lotus of the qualities beginning with Ājñā, having thus established it. (26)
I shall proclaim its sequence; listen attentively.
This supreme secret has always resided within my heart. (27)
O Goddess, O beautiful one, listen now to that which is accompanied by mantras in due order:
O Goddess, one should bring the seed-syllable and Kuṇḍalinī to the Ājñā-cakra. (28)
O Maheśānī, within that wheel, the self accompanied by the mind should recite the mantra of the fifty Mātṛkās ten times, O Dear One. (29)
There, having meditated upon the Yugma-kalā, one should satisfy it with the root mantra;
O Supreme Goddess, one should cause the life-force (jīva) to descend together with Kuṇḍalinī.
O Dear One! having united it with the mind, one should suspend it within the state of purity;
O Supreme Goddess! that most excellent phoneme of Mātṛkā is located in that wheel.
O Goddess! O Beloved! One should recite [the mantra] ten times with the mind as the charioteer;
for everything is to be accomplished by the mind, and the mind is the achiever of all goals.
There, one should satisfy the sixteen digits (kalās) situated within her with the root mantra;
O Goddess, one should cause them to descend toward the city that consists of resonance by means of the Praṇavas.
There, one should satisfy Mahādeva, the Lord of the gods, who resides therein;
one should satisfy him in his form as Śiva with the mantra consisting of the syllable Om (praṇava).
One should satisfy her, who resides there as the twelve-fold digit (kalā) and possesses a radiance equal to ten million flashes of lightning,
with the root mantra preceded by the recitation of the Mātṛkā.
One should cause Śiva to descend into the Maṇipūra and satisfy Him there;
O Goddess, one should satisfy the ten kalās situated therein with the root mantra. || 36 ||
Having first recited the Mātṛkā, one should offer libations to the supreme digit (kalā);
below that, O Supreme Goddess, one should cause it to descend into the [lower] centers (svādhiṣṭhāna).
O Great Goddess! Svādhiṣṭhāna is white, resembling a diamond;
one should satisfy the deity Śiva residing there with the root mantra. || 38 ||
O Maheśānī! One should satisfy with the Māyā-bīja the root mantra, which is the supreme and auspicious Prāsāda, and the divine six-fold Kalā residing therein. (39)
Then, O Goddess, having led the seed-syllable together with Kuṇḍalinī to the Mūlādhāra, one should diligently contemplate Śiva with the mind as the charioteer. (40)
O Dear One! One should satisfy Śiva with the root mantra and the Prāsāda mantra;
thereafter, one should satisfy the eternal Yugakalā with the root mantra.
Having recited the Mātṛkā ten times, one should always satisfy Śiva;
O Queen of the Gods! having reached her own place, Kuṇḍalī is the supreme deity.
Accompanied by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, she was thinner than a spider's thread,
resembling the color of lac and vermilion, and like the rising sun.
O beloved! [He should bring] Śiva’s worthy young bride who has assumed the form of fire;
then, O Supreme Goddess, he should bring the life-force (jīva) and the lotus (puṣkara). 44.
The lotus in the heart is always known as the abode of the individual soul (jīva);
and that, O Goddess, is the station of Brahman, resembling the orb of the sun. 45.
The Word-Brahman is the Supreme Brahman; indeed, all words abide therein.
O lady of pure smiles, the Word-Brahman has the form of a lamp-flame.
O Supreme Goddess! O Beloved! The individual soul (jīva) has the form of a lamp-flame;
it is the Śabdabrahman, the Supreme Brahman, ever endowed with Śakti.
Power resides everywhere—in the sun, fire, and moon reflected in water;
O lady of pure smiles, power resides in all the gods and goddesses as well. 48.
Everything is born endowed with power; yet the fool who does not understand this, having gone to the world of the departed spirits, is indeed reborn as a pig. (49)
Thus ends the third chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 3 ||
Now begins the fourth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: Vāmā is situated in the center of the navel, and Jyeṣṭhā is established in the heart.
And Raudrī, O Supreme Goddess! is always established upon the head. || 1 ||
O Maheśānī! Vāmā is said to be Brahmā, Jyeṣṭhā is declared to be Viṣṇu, and Raudrī is to be known as Rudra; thus the triad of points (bindus) is described.
O Supreme Goddess! O Beloved! Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra are always of the nature of Prakṛti; through the Bindu, O Dear One, they are always the performers of action.
O lady of pure smiles! The seed-syllable *bindu* belongs to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśa; by the *bindu*, O lady of pure smiles, creation and protection are brought about.
O Supreme Goddess! One withdraws the creation through the *bindu* in due order;
O Maheśānī! Without the *bindu*, O Beloved, everything is like a corpse.
Henceforth, O Great Goddess, I shall proclaim a most wonderful secret: one should recite the three-syllabled mantra ten times at the root-support (mūlādhāra).
Listen to the three-syllabled mantra, O Goddess of Devas! Attend to it with careful attention. Having extracted the seed-syllable of Śiva, enclose it within the seed-syllable of Earth. (7)
Having joined it with the bindu and ardhacandra, O lady of pure smiles, the practitioner should begin the recitation, having raised up the one who delights Śiva within the heart-lotus.
Having encapsulated it within the seed-syllable of Śiva, make it joined with the Bindu and the Half-moon;
O Supreme Goddess! extract the seed-syllable *ra* on the forehead.
O Maheśānī! Having joined the letter *ka* with the vowel *lā* (kalā), make it conjoined with the *bindu* and the half-moon (*ardha*).
These are the mantras, O Great Goddess, which are the cause of the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).
The Goddess said:
"O Lord of the gods! Let that eye of knowledge consisting of austerity be told.
O Īśāna, tell it out of compassion, if I am dear to you. (11)
O Supreme Lord! Having burned the deity situated on the left side, O Supreme Lord, the individual soul becomes pure in essence through the mind.
One should worship one's chosen deity and, with a tranquil mind, recite the mantra;
furthermore, how can sinful thought arise in a person in such a state? (13)
O Lord, this doubt dwells in my heart like a grain of rice;
O Mahādeva, O God, O treasure-house of compassion, sever this doubt of mine! (14)
The illustrious Lord said: Listen, O lotus-petal-eyed one! To this most wonderful secret.
O Goddess, by means of witherings and burnings, [one subdues] the person who is the embodiment of sin. 15.
O Supreme Goddess! having been completely consumed, it is always born again;
O Pārvatī, the Iḍā indeed always remains in the left side.
O beloved, the sin committed through the left channel resides in the left side of the abdomen;
by the mere union with the [central] channel, it cuts away the very root of that sin.
Therefore, O Great Goddess! the man with black hair is born again, O Goddess, following the ritual of recitation and worship.
Listen, O lotus-petal-eyed one! To the secret residing in the heart, which burns away all remaining sins and brings about their destruction, if you so desire. (19)
O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign! For the removal of that sin, recite this Vidyā; likewise, if you have a desire, [recite it] for Manmatha.
By reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, one is liberated from that sin;
O beautiful lady, the purification of the mind and the individual soul is achieved through breath control (prāṇāyāma).
O Great Goddess, this purification is praised in all tantras;
it applies to all Viṣṇu mantras, Śiva mantras, and those of Gaṇādhipa.
O Maheśānī! [This applies] to Śakti, Sūrya, and among the hosts of other deities as well.
Thus, O Goddess, this most wonderful secret has been told to you. (23)
The earth element is indeed the Ādhāra, and water is the Svādhiṣṭhāna, O beloved;
the fire element is Maṇipura, and the wind element is in Anāhata.
And at the throat, O Supreme Goddess, the principle of emptiness (śūnyatattva) is always remembered;
above that is the principle of mind (manastattva), and the mind is all-pervasive everywhere. (25)

O Supreme Goddess, because of its sovereignty and pervasiveness, the mind is directly composed of the *bindu*; as long as it exists, so too do the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) and the other [practices]. (26)
O Goddess of the Gods! all those [objects] are led forth by the mind alone;
for the mind is always all-pervading, all-knowing, and the witness of all. (27)
O Maheśānī, O beloved! Sin and merit have the mind as their protector.
Speech is born from the mind and is directed by the mind alone.
O Maheśānī! Mantra is knowledge; one should perform the recitation (japa) with the mind.
Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 4 ||
Then the fifth chapter.
The venerable Lord said:
O beloved, one who lives endowed with the mind is always a performer of action.
O Goddess, because the mind, when fully developed, is accompanied by the state beyond mind (unmanī). || 1 ||
And Unmanī, O Maheśānī! is the destroyer of the sins of worldly existence.
O Parameśānī! O beloved! hear now the secret reality concerning the individual soul (jīva). || 2 ||
The wise one, having drawn up the individual soul (jīva) situated at the mūlādhāra— which is shaped like the flame of a lamp— by means of the *praṇava*, should dissolve it into the dvādaśānta.
And in the ether, O Maheśānī! one shall attain the bliss of liberation;
and in the heart-lotus, O Maheśānī! there is the vision of the Supreme Brahman.
O Supreme Goddess, according to the command, first comes the vision of the Guru;
then, having gone to Maṇipūra, one should bathe it together with the mind.
Then, having gone to the Svādhiṣṭhāna, one should perform the touch of fire;
thereafter, O Maheśānī! O Dear One! one should dissolve the individual soul (jīva) into the Mūlādhāra.

O Goddess! With the mind as its charioteer, the individual soul (jīva) performs all actions—both good and evil—by means of that which transcends the mind (unmanī), which destroys worldly existence. || 7 ||
The individual soul (jīva) consists of pure being and is devoid of both good and evil karma;
O Dear One, when sin stands upon the left side of a person, [it is perceived].
In that situation, a conjunction arises where one performs improper action;
O Supreme Goddess! if such a conjunction with sin occurs, || 9 ||
Then, through the conjunction with the mind, the individual soul (jīva) performs its activity;
but O beloved, since the jīva consists of pure sattva, how could it have such activity?
O Supreme Goddess, if the mind is joined with Unmanī,
then the bearer of sin remains on the left side of the individual soul.

O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, because the mind and the state beyond mind (unmanī) emerge and submerge within the phenomenal worlds from that [source] on the right, [it is called Dakṣiṇāmūrti]. 12.

O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign! The process of transcending the mind (*unmanīkaraṇa*) occurs throughout the ten states, including the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, O Supreme Sovereign. (13)
Within the Suṣumnā is the Citrā, possessing a luster equal to ten million moons;
there, O Goddess, Kuṇḍalinī indeed performs her coming and going.
Sometimes in that month it is a lotus, sometimes a red lotus;
indeed, O beloved, sometimes it is a white lotus, and sometimes a fire-lotus.
O Maheśānī! This supreme follower of the gods, who possesses earrings, always pierces the city, goes forth, and returns again; he is beyond all worldly manifestations.
O Maheśānī, I shall tell you that which is concealed in all the tantras;
by knowing which, O Goddess, the practitioner shall attain all siddhis. (17)
Since the devotee of Viṣṇu indeed partakes in the fruits of dharma, artha, kāma, and mokṣa, I shall speak out of affection for you, O Maheśānī of pure smiles! (18)
Brahmāṇī, Caṇḍikā, Raudrī, Gaurī, Indrāṇī, as well as Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Durgā, Nārasiṃhī, and Kālikā. (19)
Śivadūtī, Vārāhī, Māheśī, Kauśikī,
as well as Śāṅkarī and Jayantī, are established upon the pure lotus.
Maṅgalā, Kapālikā, Medhā, Śivarūpikā, Śākambharī, Bhīmā, Gāṇḍā, and likewise Bhrāmarī. || 21 ||
Ambikā in the form of Rudra and Kṣamā in the form of Fire—
these, O Supreme Goddess, are always established within the heart-lotus.
Dhātrī, Vahnirūpā, Madhyamā, O lady of pure smiles!
Aparṇā, Maheśānī, as well as Vāmā and Mahodarī. (23)
Ghorarūpā Mahākālī, as well as Bhayaṅkarī and Kṣemaṅkarī, O Queen of Devas, are always stationed in Maṇipūra. (24)
O Goddess of the gods, O beloved, there are Ugracaṇḍā and likewise Caṇḍāvatī;
and also Caṇḍā and Pracaṇḍā, who are served by Caṇḍanāyaka.
And Caṇḍikā herself, O Queen of the Gods! always resides in the Svādhiṣṭhāna;
likewise, O Maheśānī, the Great Goddess exists there in the form of Māyā. (26)
Likewise Priyaṅkarī and likewise Sanātanī;
these, O Supreme Goddess, are always situated in the Mūlādhāra. (27)
O Goddess, she who takes the form of the transformer of fruits and likewise Balapramathinī always resides in the Ājñā-cakra as a pair of imperishable syllables.
But hear, O Pārvatī, the special feature of this, O Supreme Goddess;
this knowledge, O Great Goddess, is established in Sadāśiva. (29)
By the power of this knowledge, I shall withdraw the three worlds;
Viṣṇu shall be the sustainer, and Brahmā shall always be the creator.
O Goddess of the Gods! Having encased [the name] within whichever seed-syllable (bīja) was previously indicated for each respective deity, one should perform the recitation (japa) of the deities. 31.
O Goddess Pārvatī! Then the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) becomes perfected;
otherwise, O lotus-eyed one, the purification results in being like a ghost (preta).
O Goddess, one should recite the mantra of the fifty Mothers sequentially within the six cakras;
O Supreme Mistress, one should perform the recitation with diligence in the six cakras. (33)
At that very moment, great accomplishment arises even for the practitioner;
having become equal to the Kalāvṛkṣa tree, the practitioner becomes a sky-walker (khecara). || 34 ||
In that way, the practitioner becomes the substratum of the qualities beginning with *aṇimā*.
*Aṇimā* is the subtle form, and *laghimā* is the gross form. (35)
O lotus-faced one, the attainment of the state of supreme sovereignty is called the highest attainment; yet even that renown brings distress to the mind. (36)
O lotus-faced one, my greatness is sung of in all the worlds;
yet that very same greatness, O Goddess, resides within my own knowledge. (37)
O Dear One! The form that pervades the entire universe is proclaimed as Īśitva (lordship), and the form that holds the universe under its control is called Vaśitva (mastery). || 38 ||
O Goddess! This state of being under the sway of desire, which causes the destruction of Kandarpa, has been revealed through devotion to you as possessing qualities such as *aṇimā* and the rest. (39)
It must not be told to anyone, O beloved, concerning your origin;
listen, O Goddess, for I shall explain the reason for the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi). 40.
—O Maheśānī! One should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
The *tāra* (oṃ), the sky (ha), fire (ra), the goad (ṅī), and likewise light (*jyotis*)—this is remembered as the *manu*.
By the power of this knowledge, the fruit of the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) shall be attained. || 41 ||
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 5 ||
Now begins the sixth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: Listen, O Maheśānī! I shall explain to you the specific knowledge.
O Supreme Goddess, having known which, I am Śiva, the destroyer of death. || 1 ||
O Supreme Goddess! Having known which, Brahmā is always the creator of the universe;
and having known which, O lady of pure smiles, the divine Viṣṇu is the sustainer of the world.
But having known this, O Maheśānī! I am unable [to describe it], O Maheśvarī;
having known which, O Maheśānī, O Parameśvarī, one becomes the moon and the sun. (3)
O beloved, she who is of unmanifest form, beautiful, and ever accessible through yoga, illuminates the entire universe— the cosmic egg with all its moving and non-moving beings.
Always residing by taking recourse to the body, she dwells there, capable of assuming any form at will.
O Goddess of pure smiles, the body is of two kinds: the gross and the subtle. (5)
O lady of excellent countenance! Flesh, bone, hair, blood, fat, marrow, as well as feces and urine, reside in Hara;
and wind and bile are likewise joined with him.
O Goddess, I have described this which consists of the gross; now I shall tell you of the subtle:
the channel Iḍā is situated on the left, white in color, and having the form of the moon.
On the right is the one named Piṅgalā, in male form and having the nature of the Sun;
in the middle of those two, O Supreme Goddess, is Suṣumnā, whose form is Brahman.
Winding in a counter-clockwise direction like a poisonous thread,
it remains at all times pervading [the body] from the base (mūla) up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
In all the fibers [of the body], there are three channels consisting of will, knowledge, and action;
it is held that there are thirty-three million channels in the body.
Among those, ten are said to be principal; among them, three are established.
O Maheśānī! One should fill the left channel with the seed-syllable of air (Yam).
Having recited the mantra sixteen times over the wind, one should fill [the breath] by moving it counter-clockwise;
O Great Goddess, one should then retain it for sixty-four [counts] in the Maṇipūra.
O lady of pure smiles, O Great Goddess! one should recite the seed-syllable of fire through the right channel for half a *kumbhaka*, as before, within the heart-lotus, O Beloved! (13)
Having purified [the body] with the seed-syllable of wind (vāyubīja), one should burn it with the seed-syllable of fire (vahnibīja).
O beautiful lady, one should contemplate the white seed-syllable of Varuṇa upon the forehead.
Having recited [the mantra] for half a *kumbhaka*, one should indeed exhale through the right path;
thus, O Goddess, one should perform the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*) twelve times.
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī! [I have described] the extensive purification of the five elements;
O Supreme Goddess, I have also explained the previously mentioned general purification. (16)
O Supreme Goddess, this is declared to be the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) of the body;
O Beloved, this is the purification of the elements of the subtle body.
O Supreme Goddess! O Mistress of the Gods! If the mind is joined with the Unmanī state, one should cause it, along with the vital breath (jīva), to submerge into the Suṣumṇā. 18.
Through the practice of meditation and concentration, one perceives Brahman directly; of this there is no doubt.
One should recite [the mantra] with supreme devotion using a rosary of the prescribed number of beads.
O Dear One, one should meditate for a moment on the Vidyā joined with Manonmanī;
when joined with Manonmanī, one should recite the mantra at the Brahma-randhra, which is the seat of the individual soul (jīva).
Then, O fair-faced goddess, having reached the Brahmanadī and performed ablutions, Jīva becomes pure along with his attendants and retinues. (21)
O Supreme Goddess, O beloved one with lotus-like eyes, hear now the retinue of the individual soul: the two eyes, the two nostrils, the two ears, and the tongue. (22)
O Maheśānī, [worship] the hands and feet; O Priye, the secret parts and the generative organ in sequence; O Parameśānī, the navel; and O Parameśvarī, the mind. (23)
Of all the senses, the mind is everywhere the charioteer;
and the mind, O Supreme Goddess, becomes the Unmanī state which destroys worldly existence.
O Goddess, Unmanī is the charioteer; O Beloved, the ten states are devoid of qualities (nirguṇa).
O Goddess, these three are known as the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. (25)
Thereafter, O Great Goddess, the state of the Sun (Sūryāvasthā) is prescribed:
of all the sense organs, the mind is the supreme charioteer. (26)
O Goddess, because the individual soul (jīva) is the agent of both good and evil deeds, the mind is its charioteer; O Beloved, the Unmanī state always partakes in its own karma.
O Maheśānī, improper action arises from the conjunction of sin;
so too do weeping, delusion, fainting, hunger, and thirst, O lady of pure smiles. (28)
O lotus-eyed one, from the Puruṣa arises the origin of evil;
yet the Jīva is eternal, imperishable, subtle, all-pervading, omniscient, and supreme. || 29 ||
As is Brahman, so is the individual soul (jīva); like the flame of a lamp, every [individual soul], having attained the form of a lamp-flame, unfolds itself. 30.
O Supreme Goddess, having meditated in the mind upon the supreme, auspicious nāḍī— which resembles ten million suns, is like the celestial river Gaṅgā, and destroys all sins— 31.
In the midst of that, O Supreme Goddess, is Suṣumnā, who is supreme upon the earth,
manifest in the form of the Lake of Brahmā, and who sports in manifold pleasures.
She who is easily accessible, always to be worshipped, the very embodiment of Brahman, endowed with knowledge and realization, whose form is consciousness, and who is eternal. || 33 ||
O Maheśānī, she whose couch is the Supreme Brahman—she who stands at his left side, eternal, of the nature of Brahman, and composed of lightning. (34)
To the right is the goddess Piṅgalā, in male form and resembling the sun;
situated between them, O Maheśānī, she is filled with the arising of nectar.
O Great Goddess, the left channel (vāmanāḍī), which is variegated, supreme, subtle, and bestows great liberation, stands before one in the form of sleep.
But the dream state, O Supreme Goddess, is proclaimed as the Fourth (turiya), resting upon the Piṅgalā in the right [nostril]. || 37 ||
O Supreme Goddess, Suṣumnā is the eternal form of the waking state;
O Supreme Goddess, she is celebrated as the wondrous Fourth (Turiya). || 38 ||
Having become situated within the *citrā* [lotus], the living soul (*jīva*) becomes pure-minded;
the pure *jīva*, whose nature is *sattva*, should place the chosen goddess (*iṣṭadevī*) in his heart. (39)
O Maheśānī, by meditating upon [the Self] in the heart, the individual soul (jīva) becomes the Supreme Brahman;
indeed, O Maheśānī, it performs the movement back and forth three times.
This supreme secret, which is very difficult to obtain even in the world of Brahmā, must not be told to anyone who is like a beast, O lotus-eyed one. (41)
O Goddess, by revealing this, there will be a progressive loss;
O Maheśānī, take this reality to heart with diligence. (42)
O Great Goddess, Keśava alone knows this reality, which is Brahman.
O Goddess, without this reality, the perfection of mantra does not arise.
O Great Goddess, this reality consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. (43)
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī.
Now begins the seventh chapter.
The Śrī Devī said:
O Maheśāna, [tell me] the secret of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi), which is most wonderful.
Speak something else, O Great Lord, if I am dear to you.
"O Lord, if it is not told, then I shall cast off my body;
O Great God, wielder of the trident, O Master, please speak out of compassion. (2)

O Gaṇasundara, Lord of Gods, this secret is now [revealed] from my heart; O Goddess, it is not indeed a sealed secret within my heart. Out of affection for you, O Maheśānī, I speak it again and again.
O Goddess, O lotus-eyed one, it resides within the heart, in the *sampuṭa*, and at the *brahmarandhra*; whatever secrets exist here [are contained therein].
O Maheśānī, O beloved, you have always shown me great respect;
[O Goddess, this consists of] thirteen parts, joined with the Bindu and the Half-moon.
O Supreme Goddess, perform the *praṇava*, which consists of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, endowed with the three qualities and the bliss of reality; this station of Brahman is to be constantly served.
Above Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva is the Half-Yoni; above that is the Bindu, which is changeless and free from desire.
O Pārvatī, always contemplate that Bindu, O Supreme Goddess, which consists of light, is eternally served by Brahmā and the other gods, and which she bears upon her head.
My word is not otherwise: the stainless city, the Bindu, resides within my heart.
Meditate upon that Bindu, O Mistress of the Gods; what is the use of muttering prayers, O lady of pure smiles? (8)
The illustrious Lord said:
Having thus reflected in his heart, one obtains the entire fruit of worship.
O Maheśānī, in the absence of formal worship, one should meditate upon Śivā within the heart.
O Goddess, O beloved, the worshipper obtains the fruit of all worship;
what need has he for the meditation-worship? Contemplate the *bindu*, O Pārvatī. (10)
O Goddess of pure smiles, for all the senses and all the principles, the individual soul (jīva) and the state beyond mind (unmanī) exist; O Queen of the Gods, Brahman is the cause of them all.
O Goddess of the gods, O Pārvatī, whatever sense organs exist here,
all of them, O Goddess of the gods, are the supreme form of Prakṛti.
O Goddess, you are always the cause of Brahmā, having the form of Prakṛti;
O Supreme Sovereign, Prakṛti is the unmanifest and imperishable source of Brahmā.
O Supreme Goddess, for the sake of well-being, [the universe] has constantly fallen into a state of fragmentation;
O Great Goddess, without Śakti, Brahman is indeed like a corpse. (13)
Yogis always behold the stainless and formless;
the stainless one is eternally united with primordial nature (prakṛti).
O lotus-faced one, the creator is eternally and perpetually born;
for this very reason, O Maheśānī, the preeminence of Śakti is proclaimed. (15)
Infinite powers have been declared, pervading all that is moving and unmoving;
O Great Goddess, without power, the universe is like a corpse. (16)
O Supreme Goddess, that power which is celebrated as liberation, O Great Goddess, is in the form of a woman—the eternal cause. (17)
Whatever action is performed, everything dissolves into the radiant energy (*tejas*).
Śrī Īśvara said:
Listen, O Goddess of gods, I shall declare a most wonderful secret.
More delightful than the most essential of essences, it is eternally situated within the self.
Then, O Maheśānī, the individual soul (jīva) should meditate upon the supremely beautiful one, the auspicious young wife of Śiva, who is endowed with the splendor of ten million Kandarpas. || 19 ||
O Beloved, by her mere sidelong glance, Brahmā and the other gods become like inert matter;
O Goddess, one should meditate upon that supremely beautiful one according to the procedure taught in the Tantras. 20.
O Great Goddess, one should recite the desired mantra one hundred and eight times,
[visualizing] the river whose nature is Brahman flowing from the root center up to the aperture of Brahmā.
There, O Maheśānī, the living soul, having bathed in the river, is ever pure;
then, O Goddess, [it worships] Vāyu, Agni, and immediately after that, Varuṇa.
Having joined it with the half-bindu, one should always contemplate it in the mind;
O Great Goddess, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) occurs even at that very moment.
Then the individual soul, with a serene mind, shall attain subtle purity;
and of all the sense organs as well, O lady of pure smiles, it shall attain the essence of all principles.
All those subtle elements always reside within Prakṛti, O Śivā.
O Goddess, the body is said to be of two kinds: the gross and this subtle one. (25)
O Supreme Goddess, the form of Prakṛti is both subtle and gross;
having purified the subtle according to the rule, one should thereafter purify the gross. (26)
Listen, O lotus-petal-eyed one: one should meditate upon the chosen deity while living on the Brahman river, O Supreme Goddess of pure smiles. (27)
Having performed the ritual bath according to the rules, one shall always go to the city of Śiva;
thereafter, O Maheśānī, O beloved, the individual soul [resides] in the left nostril.
Having brought together one who was pure, supreme, subtle, and more slender than a spider's thread— the most beautiful woman herself in the form of fire— (29)
O auspicious lady, one should always meditate upon the Supreme Deity in Śivapura;
having gone there, O Maheśānī, one should meditate upon one's chosen deity.
O Goddess, having meditated upon Śivā, who consists of nectar, according to the procedure taught in the Tantras—
she who is eternally sixteen years of age and endowed with fresh youth— (31)
Resembling the full moon, red in hue, with eyes that are always flickering,
she is endowed with white, black, and reddish-brown [aspects], and is yellow and enveloped in blue.
Her feet, adorned with beautiful anklets and joined by various jewels,
were likewise graced at the waist by a girdle of gold and gems set with tinkling bells.
She is joined by millions of yoginīs, dwelling in manifold pleasures; she possesses the beauty of millions of gods of love and is ever-increasing through nectar. || 34 ||
O lady with wide, tremulous eyes like full-blown lotuses, having awakened the supreme Śiva and having perfumed the supreme Śiva with the fragrance of your lotus-like face. (35)
Having awakened [her], O Supreme Goddess, one should sit there, O Dear One;
by the mere union with Śakti, its [worldly] essence perishes, and from the complete union of Śiva and Śakti, bliss arises immediately. (36)
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī.
Now, the eighth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: At this time, O Goddess, the wise practitioner should recite his own vidyā.
Having recited it one hundred and eight times, one becomes accomplished; it is not otherwise. || 1 ||
With the mind as his charioteer, the individual soul has the mind as his driver;
at that moment, O Maheśānī, he [sees] the person in the form of sin. || 2 ||
O Goddess, when the individual soul, with a mind possessed of friends, reaches the city of Brahman, there is no going to the realm of evil; rather, O Beloved, it goes to the city of Sadāśiva. (3)
O Goddess, Sadāśiva’s city is known to consist of all powers; O Supreme Mistress, having meditated for a moment upon it within the six cakras, one should recite the mantra.
Thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, one should perform recitation within each of the cakras;
the supreme, divine six-cakra system is always equal to the city of Śiva.
O Supreme Goddess, within the six cakras there exists the sixfold power of men; O Goddess, he who performs the coming and going within the space of a single muhūrta [attains this].
O Supreme Goddess, he who, with a tranquil mind, performs [this] within the center of the Suṣumṇā is Śiva, he is Viṣṇu, and he is the perfected one (Siddha).
O lotus-eyed one, O Girijā, he who recites his own mantra with supreme devotion obtains the fruit of ten million worships for every single utterance.
O Goddess, what is the use of external worship? All that is merely a useless hardship; through mental recitation and japa, perfection is born.
Through mere meditation with the mind, all perfection is attained; of this there is no doubt.
O Great Goddess, internal worship is considered equal to ten million external rites.
O Supreme Goddess, O lotus-faced one, worship is indeed twofold:
subtle within and gross without; this is the doctrine of all the Āgamas, my dear. (11)
For in the case of subtle worship, O beloved, even a single [item] becomes as vast as ten million;
there is no need for purification of garments and the like, O Supreme Goddess, O lady of pure smiles. (12)
Among all external forms of worship, internal worship is prescribed;
O Great Goddess, internal worship is the contemplation of the mass of radiant energy.
O Maheśānī, [this] mass of splendor is endowed with infinite power;
O Maheśānī, the subtle worship is performed within the subtle body.
The gross worship is said here to be the two-fold worship within the gross body;
however, the subtle worship is the supreme worship, which is directly of the nature of Prakṛti.
O Supreme Goddess, that worship which consists of the female form, the embodiment of Śakti, is the worship of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest; she is the desired deity. (16)
O lotus-eyed one, whether one worships Viṣṇu or Śiva, everything indeed dissolves into the Supreme Lord, the supreme splendor. (17)
O Maheśānī, whatever food offerings or supreme lamps [are presented],
all that becomes inexhaustible through their dedication to the Supreme Splendor.
The supreme Brahman is absolute certainty; whence could there be attachment, whence could there be pleasure?
It is formless, effortless, and devoid of the senses.
For the Enchantress, O Supreme Goddess, stands pervading everything;
whatever meritorious deed is performed shall become inexhaustible. (20)
O Maheśānī, the form of Brahmā and Śakti are certain, O beloved;
yet, O Maheśānī Pārvatī, there is never any worship of him.
Therefore, O Great Goddess, Śakti is the cause of Brahmā;
and O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, she is both his effect and his constant power.
Beyond this, O Maheśānī, O beloved, there is neither effect nor cause;
for he who, O Goddess, is always unwaveringly fixed upon the Lord.
O beloved, one should constantly recite the mantra of the Lord Īśvara, who is endowed with power;
for this very reason, O Maheśānī, the supreme Śakti of Brahmā is eternal.
O Maheśānī, without Śakti, liberation is indeed not produced;
therefore, both Śakti and liberation are female in form and consist of the nature of Śakti. (25)
O Maheśānī, without devotion liberation does not arise;
O Goddess, the cause of liberation is devotion, which is exceedingly difficult to attain. (26)
Therefore, O Maheśānī, this triple world, including all that is moving and unmoving, consists of woman.
Śrī-Īśvara said: O Maheśānī, I shall now describe in sequence the purification of the six cakras.
The earth element is situated in the mūlādhāra, having the nature of the svādhiṣṭhāna.
O Goddess, water is in Maṇipūra, and likewise wind is there;
O Great Mistress, O lotus-faced one, space is in Viśuddhi.
O Maheśānī, in the Ājñā-cakra is the mind, the accomplisher of all aims;
above that, O Parameśānī, is likewise a lotus facing upwards.
O Maheśānī, Śaktipura is situated above Sadāśivapura;
having reached Sadāśivapura, which resembles pure crystal, [one attains liberation].
One should always meditate with the mind upon [the deity] who resembles a thousand suns, who is united with Mahākāla, and who is surrounded by the hosts of the Mahānandi gaṇas.
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the *Śrībhūtaśuddhitantra*, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī.
Now begins the ninth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: "Thus, having indeed perceived the individual soul as the supreme Śiva by means of the mind,"
O beautiful one, when the thrill of joy arises, the individual soul comes into being.
O Maheśānī, [he saw] Sadāśiva, resembling pure crystal,
adorned with many jewels, long-armed, and captivating to the mind.
With a face serene with happiness, always self-restrained yet fond of what is dear, adorned with earrings on his ears and graced by a necklace of jewels. || 3 ||
His body was adorned with a garland of a thousand golden lotuses;
he was Śiva, possessing eight arms, three eyes, and eyes like lotus petals.
O lotus-faced one, one should likewise meditate upon his beautiful anklet on the feet, which produces a sound like the Śabdabrahman; such is the gross body of Him that one should contemplate.
O Goddess of the gods, one should meditate upon the hundredfold life-force as Śiva above the head—
subtle, supreme, divine, effortless, and always like an insentient object.
O Maheśānī, meditation on the subtle never arises;
O Maheśānī, by performing meditation on the gross, one attains liberation.
For the form of Prakṛti is indeed gross, and meditation is dear to Prakṛti;
therefore, O Goddess with the lotus-face, having first worshipped her gross body, O Beloved.
Then, O Supreme Goddess, one should contemplate the supreme splendor;
and that splendor, O Supreme Goddess, is Nature (prakṛti), the deluder.
O Supreme Goddess, Prakṛti holds primacy in the worship of Śiva;
therefore, in all forms of worship, Śakti is said to be primary.
But when, O Supreme Goddess, one has performed meditation upon the subtle body and projected the gross form there, one should then contemplate Hari within the heart.
Then, having meditated upon Hari of massive form, with eyes like lotus petals, dark-complexioned, clad in yellow garments, and adorned with a forest garland; || 12 ||
He wears a crown and earrings, his lotus-like face is serene;
his chest is adorned with the Śrīvatsa mark and beautified by a necklace of jewels. (13)
O beloved, [meditate on Him] who shines with the Kaustubha gem, who grants boons, has long arms, subdues His enemies, possesses serene lotus-eyes, and wears anklets upon His feet.
O beautiful one, O Goddess with a lotus-like face, he constantly fills the world with the sound of the flute and lute, which is the Brahman of Sound. 15.
The illustrious Īśvara said: O Great Goddess, having contemplated the subtle form of Hari, one should practice meditation;
for the body is indeed subtle and motionless, and [the mind] is of the nature of subtle Prakṛti. (16)

Nevertheless, in the worship of Hari, the primacy of *śakti* is declared; for as it is said, O lady of pure smiles, meditation (*dhyāna*), concentration (*dhāraṇā*), and absorption (*samādhi*)— [...are subordinate to it. (17)
For every form is its own nature; my word is not otherwise.
And meditation, O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, consists in contemplating all the limbs.
Thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, there is the meditation on a single limb;
this is called *dhāraṇā*. Listen to it with reverence, O Pārvatī. (19)

O Goddess, having abandoned both meditation (dhyāna) and concentration (dhāraṇā), whatever one contemplates within the heart—this should be known as samādhi; no further deliberation is required here. || 20 ||
O lady of pure smiles, O Queen of the Gods, that which I have described as meditation (dhyāna), retention (dhāraṇa), and concentration (samādhi) is all remembered as being composed of Śakti. 21.
"O Maheśānī, O beloved, there are the subtle and the gross, as well as the two powers.
Śrī Devī said:
"O God of gods, O Mahādeva, O Supreme Lord, regarding the six cakras..."
Having performed worship and meditation in the prescribed manner, one should perform the recitation. || 22 ||
O Lord, please tell me out of compassion this supreme secret, this profound mystery that increases my joy; I am your attendant.
The illustrious Lord said: "O Goddess, O lady of pure smiles, I am your servant;
I shall tell you, O lotus-eyed one, that I cannot live for even half a moment without you."
O Goddess of pure smiles, O Supreme Sovereign, O Lady of beautiful countenance, by drinking the nectar from the lotus of your mouth, I have become auspicious, having conquered death.
"O Supreme Goddess, through union with the erotic sentiment (śṛṅgāra-rasa), I drink the Kālakūṭa poison;
even for me, it is always like the adamantine body. (26)
O Queen of the Gods, O lady of pure smiles, I am your servant both internally and externally;
O Great Goddess, having meditated upon you within as one whose form is subtle. (27)
O Supreme Goddess, one hundred thousand years have passed for me in meditation;
O Goddess, external knowledge has arisen within me, O Yoginī. (28)
And within me, O Supreme Goddess, you alone exist in a subtle form;
having beheld that pair of your feet and your face, O lady of beautiful countenance. (29)
Having abandoned the knowledge of the Self, I have indeed fallen at your feet;
O Maheśānī, listen now to my words in this manner. (30)

O Daughter of the Mountain, O Great Goddess, since you possess the state of immediate yoga regarding everything that has been taught, such as the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) and so forth, I shall now explain my own tradition to you.
The supreme *sghāgama* is knowledge, the eye conjoined with wisdom;
it is considered by consciousness, O Goddess, and is indeed the Mother of the Gods. (32)
And the Vedas, O Supreme Goddess, and whatever philosophical systems there may be, O Goddess—all of them, each distinct from the others. (33)
O Supreme Goddess, fourteen tantras as well as various other types of scriptures are constantly produced from it.
O Goddess, my own arrival is as dear to me as my life;
O Mistress of Gods, O lotus-faced one, it is established within my heart as my secret compendium.
O Maheśānī, at the very moment when I, Hara, disappeared after having meditated upon my own tradition, O Goddess, O Parameśvarī, at that very instant— || 36 ||
O Goddess, internal meditation has been taken away; my own tradition remains established in the heart.
Having withdrawn internal meditation, may there always be external vision for me. (37)
Then, O Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, having visualized my own arrival within the heart-self, I shall suddenly speak before you. (38)
Otherwise, O Supreme Goddess, I shall tell you my own scripture;
for my own scripture consists of a hundred thousand verses and contains various sciences, O lady of pure smiles. (39)
O Supreme Goddess, within the great sacrifices,
[I have composed] this supreme and meritorious scripture of my own tradition, which is of the nature of Brahman, the imperishable seed of the universe.
Listen to our own tradition, O Three-eyed One; I shall speak of it.
Among the various scriptures and branches of knowledge, our own tradition is indeed praised. (41)
O Goddess who delights in the mountains, [I have taught] my own tradition, the supreme knowledge composed of various tantras,
concerning Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Sūrya.
And likewise, O lady of pure smiles, among all the gods beginning with Agni,
and likewise in all the scriptures, the preeminence of Śakti is proclaimed; O Goddess, by means of the sequence of the conch [or by calculation], Śakti is sung of everywhere.
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the glorious Bhūtaśuddhi-tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 9 ||
Now begins the tenth chapter.
The illustrious Lord said: "O Goddess of pure smiles, the garland of forest flowers and other such ornaments are considered appropriate for Viṣṇu."
All that, O Supreme Goddess, is of the nature of Śakti and nothing else. || 1 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should meditate within the thousand-petaled lotus, the city of power;
there, one should diligently practice the unification of the individual soul and Brahman.
Then one should perform meditation according to what is established in one's own scripture;
and, O Supreme Goddess, one should perform the recitation mentally.
Having become composed, one should recite with a rosary according to the prescribed number of syllables;
then, having led [the deity] to the city of the command, one should meditate upon the chosen deity.
O Goddess of the Gods, by meditating and reciting [the mantra], one becomes manifest as the Preceptor of the Suras;
O Goddess of the Gods, one should cause the mind to descend upon the Viśuddha [cakra] by means of the Vidyā.
That pure and supreme lotus of six wheels is reached;
O Supreme Goddess, having meditated upon Śivā, who consists of the universe, within the six wheels.
She who possesses the brilliance of ten million flashes of lightning, whose form is the cosmic egg,
the auspicious Śivā— desireless, immovable, delightful, supreme, and consisting of the great yoga.
The supreme goddess who deludes all the gods, who is endowed with the purpose of bliss,
who consists of poisonous threads, yet is herself the manifest form of nectar.
O beloved Supreme Goddess, having visualized the worthy young consort of Śiva within the pure abode, one should mentally recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, O dear one.

O Goddess of gods, one should not sleep while facing the heart-lotus; rather, one should practice the supreme, transcendent pure meditation upon the supreme [deity] situated within the yoga-lotus of the castes.
O Great Goddess, within the lotus of yoga, one should contemplate in the mind the supreme Kundalini, the eternal Goddess in the form of a serpent. 11.

O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one, one should again recite [the mantra] eight hundred times on the path of yoga, [focusing on her] who is of unmanifest form, beautiful, and attainable through meditation. 12.
O beloved, one should not sleep with the vital breath and mind directed toward Maṇipūra;
[one should contemplate] Maṇipūra, which possesses great luster and resembles a serpent or a bee. 13.
There, one should unite the supreme Kuṇḍalinī with the Śiva-liṅga situated therein;
then, O Maheśānī, the individual soul attains Brahman at that very moment.
Then, O Supreme Goddess, the individual soul, enveloped by the mind, having meditated upon the pure one consisting of Brahman, should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, O Beloved. (15)
Thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, one should dissolve the Svādhiṣṭhāna into Parā;
O Great Goddess, the Svādhiṣṭhāna is like pure crystal. (16)
O Pārvatī, having united him with the supreme, divine Śiva, one should meditate there upon the Lord of Gods, whose radiance is equal to a conch shell and a jasmine flower. 17.
O Supreme Goddess, perform everything with effort through the mind;
for the mind is everywhere proclaimed to be the foremost of the senses. (18)
There, having meditated for a moment with the mind upon the god Śiva, who is peaceful and consists of the supreme Brahman, one should likewise recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
Thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, one should proceed further from the Mūlādhāra;
O Great Goddess, the Anus-lotus is proclaimed as the Mūlādhāra. (20)
One should meditate upon the Supreme Lord, who possesses a beautiful form like the rising sun, endowed with four petals, and whose body has the hue of the ocean or Varuṇa. 21.
Having united with the supreme, eternal, fruitless [reality] whose nature is knowledge,
the individual soul becomes identical with Brahman through the mere union with Śiva.
Having become composed in mind, one should likewise recite it one hundred and eight times.
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī. || 10 ||
Now, the eleventh chapter.
The venerable Lord said: "O Goddess, he who thus performs the coming and going in twelve ways,"
O beloved, he is perfected, he is the one who has gone [to liberation], and he is always equal to me.
O Goddess of gods, O fair-faced one, by mere speech his knowledge indeed becomes perfected, as do the seven crores of vidyās and mantras.

O Goddess, O Beloved, this reality concerning the *siddha*, *mādhyama*, and other [levels] is most secret; it must not be disclosed, O Beloved, and should always be hidden from the uninitiated (*paśu*).
O Goddess of gods, within my heart resides the Ajapā mantra enclosed in a casket;
it is the casket of all men and women, containing the Haṃsa bird.
O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, the Vidyās and Mantras emerged;
by the grace of Śakti, O Queen of the Gods, a hundred thousand years then passed.
O Maheśānī, O lady of pure smiles, for a hundred thousand years I have meditated upon the supreme Vidyā within the *sampuṭa*, who is the very embodiment of all Vidyās.
She who has the form of a man, yet is the form of primordial nature (prakṛti), possessing a radiance equal to the moon and sun;
she who is the mother of the Vedas, eternally chaste, a Yoginī whose very essence is Yoga.
I perpetually bow to the Goddess who carries one across the ocean of saṃsāra, the bestower of great liberation, who is eternally pure, eternal, and possesses a manifest form.
Having prostrated before the supreme, divine [goddess], O lady of pure smiles, I shall speak;
the Lord said:
"After raising up the one named Kāñcana, one should then raise up Romañca."
O beloved, having extracted the essence of mercury, one should thereafter [extract] gold.
Having formed it joined with the Bindu and Ardha-chandra, one should perform the recitation upon the six lotuses;
having recited one hundred and eight times upon the six lotuses, O lotus-eyed one.
Or one may recite it ten times and obtain the fruit of the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi);
however, having performed it once, one should carry out the purification of the elements.
O Great Goddess, O Beloved, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) must then be performed along with its ancillaries;
otherwise, O Beloved, worship is fruitless and recitation is fruitless.
O Goddess, by reciting the syllables of the *yuga*, one obtains the fruit of the four ages;
O Goddess, whatever fruit men obtain from the recitation of the four ages— [that fruit is attained]. (13)
O Pārvatī, one obtains that fruit by a single recitation;
O Goddess of the Gods, there is no doubt that my satisfaction is achieved by a single recitation. (14)
O Supreme Goddess, O Śivā, having constantly contemplated the *sampuṭa*—which is eternal and the embodiment of all things—one should always meditate upon the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*), O Goddess. (15)
O Goddess of gods, having worshipped one [form], we worship the Great Vidyā;
otherwise, O Supreme Mistress, O fair-faced one, [we worship] the Great Vidyā. (16)
Thereafter, O Supreme Goddess, we worship the Great Vidyā;
otherwise, O Supreme Goddess, everything would become like a corpse. (17)
The illustrious Lord said: O Maheśānī, O beloved, I shall speak again of another tantra;
I will explain the tantra of tantras, how the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) is to be performed. 18.
O Goddess, O lady of excellent countenance, the cause of evil is a man joined with sin, possessed of anger and delusion, dark-complexioned and slightly tawny. (19)
I shall describe its purification, O lady with large, lotus-like eyes;
for there is no purification of even the five vital airs, O beautiful-faced one. (20)
O lotus-faced one, this body, composed of the five elements, is by its very nature eternally pure; yet it experiences weeping, as well as fainting and delusion.
O lotus-faced one, [this] arises from the Person who is of the nature of sin;
O beloved, listen as I recite the mantras for the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi). 22.
O Goddess, O Pārvatī, the Praṇava is threefold: Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, and Raudrī;
thus it is of three kinds, O Maheśānī of beautiful countenance. (23)
Having placed the *praṇava* at the beginning and the end, one should recite the fifty *mātṛkās*.
Having joined them with the *bindu* and the half-moon (*ardhacandra*), this is the *vidyā* that liberates one from existence. (24)
For she is the mother of all mantra-sciences, O lady of pure smiles, and he is the father;
indeed, both the father and the mother are the *mātṛkā* of all mantra-sciences. (25)
If the father and mother are satisfied, the anger of others is useless;
for he who performs the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) without understanding its ancient [significance]. || 26 ||

O Goddess of gods, O fair-faced one, his purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) is fruitless; O Great Sovereign, they do not approve of his recitation or worship if he lacks the purification of the elements.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī. || 11 ||
Now, the twelfth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: "O Great Goddess, O Beloved, he who would constantly practice this knowledge..."
Even he, a great lord of yoga, is equal to me; of this there is no doubt.
O Parameśvarī, O Goddess of gods, all his mantras and vidyās will be swiftly perfected; there is no need for deliberation in this matter.
This is the supreme secret, the eternal determination of Brahman;
it is the knowledge of Yoga, austerity, the scriptures, learning, and whatever arts there may be.
For everything is the form of primordial nature; this is my firm word.
Listen, O Pārvatī, I shall speak the supreme secret.
O Maheśānī, I shall proclaim the Vidyā of Bhūtaśuddhi, which is most closely guarded; listen, O wise one with large, lotus-like eyes. (5)
The illustrious Lord said: O Goddess, one must certainly meditate upon the Vidyā named Bhāgavatī;
O Maheśānī of pure smiles, having uttered the seed-syllable of desire (Klīm) three times.
Then, O Goddess, one should utter "dhīmahi" followed by the wife of fire (svāhā);
thereafter, O Supreme Mistress, one should extract the threefold kāma-mantra.
O Goddess, because this belongs to the Bhagavatī, it is remembered as Bhāgavata;
one should perform the recitation of this great vidyā named Bhāgavatā ten times.
O Goddess, Supreme Sovereign, if a human being recites this mantra day after day,
he shall obtain the very fruit of initiation.
O Great Goddess, this is the eternal rite, the Vidyā known as Bhāgavatī—
a Vidyā resembling a wish-fulfilling tree that bestows dharma, kāma, artha, and mokṣa.
O Supreme Goddess, in all the Vedas and Tantras, the Vidyā known as Bhāgavatī is sung of; she is eternal and has the form of primordial nature (prakṛti).
Therefore, O Great Goddess, O lotus-eyed one, whether out of ignorance, delusion, or desire, [one may recite] the Vidyā known as Bhāgavata. (12)
O Goddess of gods, if a twice-born man does not recite [the mantra], he shall attain the status of a Śūdra;
O Goddess, everything of his becomes futile—whence the worship, whence the happiness? (13)
O lady of excellent hips, even a Kṣatriya who is base does not attain [the higher state] if he does not recite it;
a Vaiśya suddenly attains the status of a Vaiśya, and a Vaiśya would reach the status of a Śūdra. (14)
O lady of excellent limbs, O Supreme Goddess, even a Kṣatriya who recites this with single-minded devotion suddenly attains the status of a Brāhmaṇa.
But the Vaiśya, O Supreme Goddess, attains the status of a Kṣatriya at that very moment;
even the Brāhmaṇa, the best of men, becomes manifest Brahman—of this there is no doubt. (16)
But a Śūdra, O Supreme Goddess, O Pārvatī, attains the status of a Vaiśya;
this knowledge, O lady of excellent hips, is always designated as Bhāgavata. (17)
O Maheśānī, O Supreme Goddess, he who recites a Purāṇa without knowing this eleven-syllable mother-mantra (vidyā) [is a fool]. (18)
He goes to a terrible hell together with that associate;
therefore, O Goddess of the Gods, that twice-born man must be avoided with great effort. (19)
The Goddess said:
"O Supreme Lord, O Bull-bannered One, a Śūdra has no entitlement [to this].
How could a Śūdra utter the Vidyā joined with the wife of Fire (the Svāhā-mantra)? (20)
The illustrious Lord said:
O Goddess, O beautiful one, one should constantly recite the Praṇava as taught in the Tantras, along with the Vahnijāyā; O Goddess, no doubt should be entertained in this matter. (21)
O Goddess Pārvatī, if one is born endowed with the Śakti-vidyā, O Goddess, then if one should suddenly recite it, accomplishment (siddhi) arises. || 22 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should not recite the Bhāgavata name joined with the syllables of the Gāyatrī;
listen now to the Bhāgavata lore for a Śūdra.
O Goddess of beautiful countenance, having extracted the three-fold Manmatha and having placed the first and the fourteenth [letters], she herself takes the form of the Praṇava.
O Supreme Goddess, if one places the wife of Vahni (the letter 's') at the end and recites it ten times,
even a Śūdra attains the status of a Vaiśya at that very moment.
At that very moment, O lotus-eyed one, great perfection is attained by the Śūdra;
know this Bhāgavata knowledge to be your own sacred tradition, O Pārvatī. (26)
O lotus-eyed one, out of affection for you, I have fully declared this supreme Svāgama, which is the Brahman endowed with infinite power and most secret to conceal.
O Maheśānī, O Goddess of beautiful countenance, I shall relate to you, the Śūdra, the entirety of the Vidyā named Bhāgavata, which is the essence of all essences. 28.
Having extracted the three *manmathas*, one should then take the syllable *dhī*;
having placed the wife of fire (*svāhā*) at the end, one should extract the three *manmathas* once more.
"This Bhāgavatī Vidyā is ordained to be recited by Śūdras;
thus has the truth been told to you with great devotion, O fair-faced one. (30)
O Goddess, if one desires one's own happiness, this should be taught to someone who is peaceful, upright, and possesses devotion even toward those of the Cāṇḍāla caste. (31)
O Maheśānī, one should not cause it to be given to a Brahmin who is not a devotee;
O Kamalekṣaṇā, one should not give it even to sons who are not devotees.
O lady of beautiful countenance, one should impart this knowledge to a devotee whose mind is tranquil;
if one gives it even to sons who are not devoted, one shall meet with death therein.
O Goddess, whatever is seen in the three worlds, including all that is moving and unmoving—
O Supreme Sovereign, it is certain that all of this is endowed with Śakti.
O Great Goddess, the Supreme Power who deludes is the essence of all reality;
those principles such as form and the rest—those very principles are Kuṇḍalinī.
For form, O Goddess, is determined to be sixfold in all tantras;
likewise, O Svāhā, taste is determined to be sixfold, consisting of various flavors. (36)
For scent, O Goddess, O Beloved, is endowed with all powers;
as are the other principles, O Beautiful One, which number twenty-four. (37)
O lotus-eyed one, O wise one, everything consists of power (śakti) in its successive stages:
white, red, yellow, green, and black.
The colors are proclaimed in succession as being diverse, with black color being the first;
O Goddess, the taste is of two kinds: fragrant and foul-smelling.
In this way, O beloved, one should always understand everything to be composed of Śakti.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter in the *Śrībhūtaśuddhi-tantra*, in the dialogue between Hara and Gaurī.
Now begins the thirteenth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: "Now, O Goddess of gods, O beloved, I shall proclaim the Vidyā consisting of Śakti."
O Goddess with the face of a lotus, having first extracted the Praṇava, || 1 ||
Then, having extracted Kāma, one should extract Praṇava immediately after that;
then, having extracted Praṇava, one should extract the Māyā-bīja.
Having uttered the Praṇava once more, listen, O Goddess of beautiful countenance;
having extracted the seed-syllable of desire (Kāma-bīja), one should then extract the Praṇava. || 3 ||
Then, O fair-faced one, having extracted Māyā (and the extraction of *vitta*),
thereafter, O Maheśānī, O beloved, one should extract Kandarpa.
Having placed the Fire-Woman (Vahni-lalanā) at the very end, one should begin the recitation;
O Supreme Goddess, this is the seventeen-syllable Vidyā.
O Supreme Goddess, the ten Vidyās are highly praised among the Vaiṣṇava, Gāṇapatya, Śaiva, and Śākta traditions, O Sovereign Lady. (6)
O beloved, O lady of excellent limbs, this vidyā consists of all powers;
if a base person does not recite this vidyā which consists of all powers, [he is lost]. (7)
O Goddess, all of that is in vain; there shall be loss at every subsequent step.
O Maheśānī, his worship is in vain, and his recitation of mantras (japa) shall likewise be in vain.
O Pārvatī, his nyāsa is fruitless, as is his purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi);
likewise, O Maheśānī, his breath control (prāṇāyāma) and his ritual sipping of water (ācamana), O beloved, are likewise in vain.
O lotus-faced one, all of that becomes fruitless for him;
therefore, O beloved, one should first recite the seventeen-syllable vidyā.
O Goddess of gods, if one knows [the mantra], one should not recite it [without first] performing worship;
this applies to all scriptures, O Goddess of gods, and especially to those of the Vaiṣṇava tradition. (11)
O Maheśānī, at the beginning, one should perform the tenfold recitation of the Vidyā, which is praised as being of the nature of Śakti in both the Śaiva and Gāṇapatya traditions. 12.
Then the practitioner should commence all the rites beginning with the purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*).
The venerable Lord said:
"Having thus performed the purification of the elements, one should perform the deposition of the *mātṛkā*."
Thereafter, O Great Goddess, O fair-faced one, [perform] prāṇāyāma. (13)
O Goddess, one should not perform worship without breath control (prāṇāyāma).
Having performed three rounds of breath control, one should then take up the postures (āsanas). || 14 ||
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 13 ||
Now begins the fourteenth chapter:
He who does not know the meaning of the mantra, the consciousness of the mantra, and its source (yoni),
his vidyā will not be accomplished even by a hundred million recitations.
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, this secret previously indicated—this very reality, O Mahādeva, O Śaṅkara, please tell me out of compassion. (2)
The illustrious Lord said:
O Supreme Goddess, listen attentively to the meaning of the mantra, as well as the consciousness of the mantra, which is the supreme state of Nirvāṇa. (3)
In this context, O Supreme Goddess, I shall speak at your command:
one should meditate upon the root-mantra as one's chosen deity within the *mūlādhāra*.
One should meditate upon the Supreme Immutable, resembling pure crystal;
one should meditate upon the eternal, desired Vidyā, which is a series of syllables.
Having meditated upon this for half a muhūrta, one should become intent on the fivefold meditation;
O Maheśānī, after performing that meditation for another half a muhūrta, [one should proceed].
Then, O Maheśānī, O lotus-eyed one, the individual soul (jīva), having gone from there to the Svādhiṣṭhāna by means of the mind, should meditate upon the chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā). || 7 ||
Having visualized the auspicious series of syllables, resembling the Bandhūka flower and red as Japā or vermilion, situated within the center of a lotus.
Then the soul, with a serene mind, together with the bird and Sundarī,
having gone from there to Maṇipūra, should meditate upon the chosen deity.
He beheld the supreme series of syllables situated within the center of a lotus,
resembling pure crystal, resting upon the chest of Śiva.
Then, O Maheśānī, O Pārvatī, O you with long lotus-like eyes, the individual soul quickly went to the heart-lotus along with the bird. 11.
Thus, O Great Goddess, one should meditate upon the Vidyā upon a lotus;
having visualized the row of syllables possessing the luster of great emeralds. (12)
