Then, O beloved Pārvatī, the soul, having entered that dense lotus, proceeded in a purified state, like the life-force of a bird, O lady of excellent limbs.
O Great Goddess, one should visualize the desired Vidyā above the ether;
having visualized it as a row of syllables, O fair-faced one, it is green in color. (14)
There, O Goddess Pārvatī, O Queen of Devas, O Khajjana-eyed one of pure smiles, Jīva went to the city of Ājñā along with the bird. 15.
O Great Goddess, having visualized the desired Vidyā as the manifest embodiment of Brahman itself,
one should contemplate the series of syllables colored by the four phonemes.
O woman of excellent complexion, having contemplated and meditated upon the wheels of command, O Supreme Goddess, having performed meditation upon the six wheels, O lady of pure smiles. (17)
O Supreme Goddess, O Pārvatī, know that very form which is manifested through meditation to be the meaning of the mantra. (18)
Then, having transcended all attachments, the living soul, together with the bird, proceeded to the supremely delightful state of Nirvana, the highest station. (19)
Within that [city] is the thousand-spoked city of Śiva; in its center, O Goddess, beloved, is the city of Kauśikī, which is composed of pure sattva and consists of Śakti.
O Goddess of the gods, having visualized the series of imperishable syllables which are nectar and an elixir, the individual soul indeed departs swiftly along with the bird.
O lotus-faced one, that beautiful city of Śiva is eternally situated at the foot of a wish-fulfilling tree (kalpavṛkṣa), strewn with various jewels; its very foundation is there.
And the tree, O Supreme Goddess, is eternally composed of the three qualities;
the tree consists of the five elements and is endowed with five branches. (23)
O lady of pure smiles, it is a flower with four branches, possessing the four Vedas, endowed with the reality of the wheel, and joined with the four castes— white and red in color.
O Maheśānī, listen to the two supreme flowers—the yellow and the black—and also the green one, O Maheśānī, which is variegated and deludes all. (25)
And this, O Great Goddess, is remembered as the sixfold merit;
as for those other branches which are minor, O Blue-eyed One, [they are not so]. (26)
All those leaves are all the scriptures, O beautiful one; and the bark, bones, marrow, and pith are the branches of the tree, my dear. (27)
All these, O Queen of the Gods, are proclaimed as the senses;
they consist of all powers, O Goddess, divine one with eyes like blue lotuses. (28)
Such was that great tree, adorned with bees;
all the Itihāsas and Purāṇas were situated upon that tree. (29)
O Supreme Goddess, it was adorned with cuckoos and many other birds;
it was delightful, filled with various species of birds, and joined by hosts of divine women.
O lotus-faced one, it is adorned by gods, dānavas, and gandharvas;
O Goddess, it is graced by kinsmen and by hosts of attendants who long for jewels and other treasures. (31)
For it is subtle, supreme, divine, a couch that deludes all;
O Goddess, it is equal to ten million moons and possesses a radiance equal to ten million suns.
It was joined with the rays of the cool-rayed moon, gladdened by various fragrances,
adorned with clusters of diverse flowers, and encircled by a golden garland.
Thereafter, O Maheśānī, Sadāśiva himself,
O Goddess Pārvatī, should again meditate there as the individual soul (jīva) joined with a bird.
O Maheśānī, Sadāśiva is joined with Mahākuṇḍalinī;
having thus meditated upon the wish-fulfilling tree (kalpadruma), one should [meditate] on the jeweled altar beneath it.
There above, O Maheśānī, O beloved, one should meditate upon the couch, joined by ten million beautiful women, with chowries held in their hands. (36)
O lady of pure smiles, having thus constantly meditated upon the living soul in the mind,
O Maheśānī, O lotus-faced one, whatever is desired by each individual— 37.
O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, his vital breath, joined with meditation and intent upon contemplation, should mentally recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times.
O Goddess of gods, having sequentially enclosed the syllables of the mantra within the *mātṛkā*, the practitioner, with a tranquil soul, should recite it one hundred and eight times, O beloved. (39)
One should perform this with supreme effort both in direct and reverse order;
O Goddess, O beautiful one, know that consciousness arises through this sequence. 40.
The meaning of the mantra and the consciousness of the mantra have been told to you out of devotion;
it must not be spoken to anyone if one desires one's own welfare. (41)
This supreme secret is to be kept strictly hidden, O fair-faced one;
one should reveal it only to a disciple who is endowed with devotion and is a true practitioner (sādhaka).
O Great Goddess, one should also bestow consciousness upon the Vaiṣṇava;
O Great Goddess, they worship both with the Viṣṇu-mantra and the Śiva-mantra. (43)
O lotus-faced one, a Vaiṣṇava should diligently practice the mantra Caitanya with many jewels; thereby the mantra and the vidyā shall become perfected.
He who possesses a perfected mantra becomes Śiva himself; of this there is no doubt.
That practitioner shall roam within the vessel of the cosmic egg (Brahmāṇḍa). 45.
O Maheśānī, one hundred crores [of recitations] is remembered as its *puraścaraṇa*.
O Goddess, he who recites it devoid of consciousness is not a doer of sin. (46)
The meaning of the mantra and the consciousness of the mantra are to be well-guarded secrets throughout the three worlds;
yet, out of devotion to you, O beautiful one, I have declared them, for I am your servant.
O Goddess, O beautiful one, by your grace I am the conqueror of death;
O lotus-faced one, through drinking the nectar from the lotus of your mouth. 48.
My body is like a vajra, eternally increasing in manifestation;
O Goddess, the entire universe is always composed of your form. (49)
O Supreme Goddess, you are eternally that Power;
O Great Goddess, full of compassion, you are Prakṛti residing within the body.
O beloved Supreme Goddess, you who were Satī have now become Pārvatī;
O beloved, having attained supreme chastity, you are now Pārvatī.
O Maheśānī, O beautiful one, since you abandoned your affection for Satī and became Pārvatī, O auspicious lady of pure smiles, you have entered the womb of Menakā. (52)
In the meantime, O beautiful one, remaining constantly devoted to meditation, I remain here having attained this state of contemplation.
Devoted to the path of meditation, I perform the recitation of my own scripture, which is my own abode in the form of power (śakti) that eternally resides within the heart. (54)
O Pārvatī, O Goddess of gods, within one's own abode there are various clusters of colors;
among these various colors, O Goddess, ten colors are proclaimed.
O Goddess, having recited these— your own scripture, the essence of essences, higher than the highest—
for a hundred thousand years, [one realizes] your own scripture in the form of Śakti.
O Great Goddess, O Supreme Sovereign, having attained perfection through your own scripture, they have abandoned the path of meditation and sing [only] at your feet. 57.
Whatever is desired by way of the path of meditation, all that I shall tell you;
for indeed, O Goddess, my dear, nothing exists without one's own scripture (svāgama).
For the entire cosmic egg, O Supreme Goddess, is established within one's own scripture;
and from that scripture, millions of sacrificial fires are produced.
O Goddess, O Beloved, millions of cosmic eggs were created according to my own scripture;
O Maheśānī, there are also various Purāṇas and Tantras.
O Goddess of pure smiles, whatever is seen, whether gross or subtle—O Supreme Sovereign with a lotus-like face, all that [is described] according to our own scripture. (61)
O Goddess with the lotus face, Brahmā performs the act of creation according to his own scripture; O daughter of the mountain, Viṣṇu performs the act of preservation according to his own scripture.
I withdraw the entire universe, the three worlds with all that is moving and unmoving;
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Rudra—all of them in the form of their own scriptures.
One's own tradition is the form of Brahman; one's own tradition is the supreme state.
It is a mass of splendor, O Maheśānī, as has been said, O lotus-faced one. (64)
O Goddess of gods, O beloved, she is a mass of splendor in the form of a woman who has come to me;
she is my own arrival, liberation, absolute freedom, and the imperishable state of nirvāṇa.
O Goddess, let there be a welcome for all, including gods, asuras, and humans;
O Supreme Mistress, O Beloved, a welcome is always dear to me.
This secret, endowed with my own tradition, has been told by me in the course of the discussion.
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 14 ||
Now begins the fifteenth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: [This practice] is auspicious, conducive to fame and longevity, and it destroys the impurities of the Kali age.
He who performs the Mātṛkā-nyāsa is indeed the illustrious Sadāśiva himself. || 1 ||
O Great Goddess, he who recites the letters of the Mātṛkā without performing the ritual placement (nyāsa) goes to a terrible hell; obstacles beset him at every step.
Even Brahmā and the other gods, having performed this [worship], are the agents of creation, preservation, and dissolution;
and Kṛṣṇa, the leader of Dvārakā, having performed it as well, [attains his goals] age after age.
O Supreme Goddess, O lotus-faced one, by resorting to the letters of the Mātṛkā, Śrī Kṛṣṇa became the enchantor of women through this [mantra]. || 4 ||
O Maheśānī, O fair-faced one, Śrī Rāma took delight with sixteen thousand women for the sake of his mother in Ayodhyā.
O Goddess of the gods, one who is devoted to vigor enjoys a kingdom free of thorns;
Rāma ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.
Having slain the three kinds of heroes— the elephants, the night-stalkers, and others—
the best of the Raghus, relying upon the phonemes of the Mātṛkā, shall accomplish everything.

O Goddess, the wise practitioner should perform everything regarding the goddess Mātṛkā, who consists of fifty letters, the mother who deludes the universe, according to the previously mentioned Tantra.
O lady of pure smiles, first perform the meditation upon the Mātṛkā-gāyatrī with full concentration;
thereafter, the practitioner should diligently perform the recitation (japa) of the Mātṛkā.
O Goddess, one should then, with a concentrated mind, perform the pair of six-limbed [practices];
thereafter, the meditation on the Mātṛkā and then the external nyāsa.
Thereafter, O Great Goddess, [one should perform] the supreme drinking of the Mātṛkās;
thus, O Goddess, one should perform the eighth [rite], the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
Having recited the armor-mantra (kavaca), O Goddess, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon the limbs;
for this supreme nyāsa, O Supreme Mistress, the Guru is the very embodiment of the deity.

O Great Goddess, I shall tell you that which has not been stated in all the tantras as it arises in this context; listen as I describe the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the three qualities (triguṇa). 13.
O Supreme Goddess, without which [the mantra] is useless—[it is that which is] joined with Śiva, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā, and united with the Bindu and the Half-moon. || 14 ||
O Goddess of pure smiles, Rajas, Sattva, and Tamas are the three half-yonis;
O Great Sovereign, above them all is the Bindu, whose nature is Brahman. || 15 ||
And one should perform the placement (nyāsa) endowed with the three qualities (guṇas) upon its joints;
one should carry out the triple placement in the locations of the fifty Mātṛkās.
Then, O Goddess of the gods, meditate upon the placement (nyāsa) that fascinates the three worlds;
O Supreme Sovereign, this secret of the placement is most wonderful. (17)

O Maheśānī, one should place the three qualities upon the petals of the conceptual elaborations (prapañcas); O Parameśānī, the movement [of the thread] becomes threefold by means of winding it in three ways.
O Goddess, one should then place the threefold [mantra] eight times in the thousand-spoked [lotus];
O Goddess, one should place the threefold [mantra] one hundred and eight times in the Bhinnā [lotus].
O Goddess of gods, by that he becomes a practitioner (sādhaka) entitled to the ritual of nyāsa;
merely by performing the triple nyāsa, he is proclaimed to be one who possesses authority.
Otherwise, the ritual placement (nyāsa) would be fruitless and the recitation (japa) would likewise become fruitless.
O Goddess, various types of nyāsa are proclaimed in numerous tantras. (21)
O Dear One, the supreme meditation on the Mātṛkā is always cherished by Brahmā and the other gods;
O Supreme Goddess, among all ritual placements (nyāsas), the Mātṛkā is the enchantress of the universe.
And the Creator, O Supreme Goddess, is praised in the Āgamas, O Dear One;
therefore, O Goddess, one should diligently perform the nyāsa of the Mātṛkās.
This is the supreme, divine secret regarding the ritual of the placement of the three qualities (guṇas);
beyond this is the sixfold [placement] of the Mātṛkā, which bestows liberation.
He who performs another nyāsa without first performing the sixfold Mātṛkā-nyāsa finds his sixfold rite to be fruitless, and the Mātṛkā becomes fruitless for him. (25)
O Supreme Goddess, whatever rites one performs after having performed the ritual placements (nyāsa), they will always be fruitful for him; otherwise, there is only weeping in the forest.
Therefore, O Goddess of beautiful countenance, listen with diligence to the Ṣoḍhā;
for the Ṣoḍhā, O Supreme Goddess, is the very embodiment of Brahman itself. (27)
Whether without letters or with letters, possessing a radiance equal to ten million moons, praised by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, beautiful, and situated within my *sampuṭa* [enclosure]. || 28 ||
O lady of excellent limbs, listen attentively to this auspicious Mātṛṣoḍhā-vidyā, which is like my own life-breath, manifestly composed of light. 29.
O Dear One, I shall explain to you in this context the sequence of the mantra beginning with Oṃ,
having encased the fifty Mātṛkās within the three qualities (guṇas).
O Goddess of the gods, by means of another effort, [one should perform this] in the fifty junctions of the locations;
first in direct order (anuloma), and immediately thereafter in reverse order (viloma).
Thereafter, O lady of excellent hips, one should perform the triple assignment (nyāsa) three times;
having performed it one hundred and eight times, one shall become a master of all supernatural powers (siddhis). || 32 ||
O Goddess of gods, by the mere act of nyāsa, a man becomes liberated while living.
O Goddess, one should first perform the nyāsa upon the petals of the worlds (prapañca).
Thereafter, O Maheśānī, one should perform the external placement (bāhyanyāsa).
But a Śūdra, O Parameśānī, should place the fourteenth vowel.
O Goddess, one should first perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) even without the armor (kavaca);
the meritorious fourteenth vowel is called the long praṇava.
Therefore, in all cases, the Śūdra is said to utter the long praṇava. || 35 ||
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the Śrī Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 15 ||
Now begins the sixteenth chapter.
The venerable Lord said: O Maheśānī, I shall describe *prāṇāyāma* to you in this context.
This is remembered as the purification of the soul, the purification of the mind, and breath control (prāṇāyāma). || 1 ||
O Supreme Goddess, one should practice the two-fold prāṇāyāma;
O Goddess, without prāṇāyāma, one should perform neither worship nor recitation.

O lady of excellent countenance, breath control (prāṇāyāma) is both with seed (sagarbha) and without seed (vigarbha). O lotus-faced one, that which is joined with recitation, meditation, and so forth, is "with seed."
O Goddess, likewise, it will certainly become devoid of color and empty;
O Supreme Sovereign, one should fill it with sixteen breaths through the iḍā.
O Dear One, one should hold [the breath] for sixty-four [counts] while it is situated in the middle of the *citrā* [channel];
one should always exhale through the middle channel with half of the *kumbhaka*.
Thus, O Goddess, one should practice breath control (prāṇāyāma) twelve times;
O Maheśānī, breath control is always composed of the Great Yoga.
O Great Goddess, without yoga, the perfection of mantra does not arise;
the union of each pair [of letters] is the cause for the complete attainment of Brahman.
In this way, O Goddess, one should always practice yoga with the mind;
and according to whichever deity it may be, [one should contemplate] their ornaments and vehicles.
One should contemplate that very [deity] during its worship through inhalation (pūraka) and the other [breath-controls],
O Goddess, daughter of the mountain— namely, inhalation, retention (dhāraka), and exhalation (recaka).
O Goddess, it is certain in all the Tantras that [the Supreme] consists of all powers;
in the Vedanta, Brahman is determined [to be such]. || 10 ||
O Goddess of gods, in the Vaiśeṣika system the atom (paramāṇu) is proclaimed;
and in the Nyāya, O Supreme Goddess, the Lord (Īśvara) is accepted as the object of placement (nyāsa).
O Goddess, through such investigation, the ritual action of Brahman is proclaimed regarding the Puruṣa who possesses a deceptive form.
O beloved, at the beginning of the Vedas, the fourth consciousness is constantly sung; even before that, O Goddess of gods, exists the eternal, hidden Brahman.
Indeed, it is devoid of senses, motionless, and stands as if directly asleep;
O Great Goddess, all this is the form of a corpse, devoid of senses. (14)
O Supreme Goddess, for all [beings], Śakti is of the nature of Prakṛti;
therefore, among all the gods, the preeminence of Śakti is proclaimed. || 15 ||
I always bow to that Śakti, the Kuṇḍalinī, the mother of all, who consists of a hundredfold revolutions, for the sake of the welfare of my own self, O lotus-eyed one. (16)
Therefore, O Goddess, without Śakti, Brahmā and the others are like corpses;
indeed, O lady of pure smiles, among all the gods, the state of being a corpse exists only in the absence of Śakti.
O beloved, the Supreme Brahman always approaches [the devotee] in the form of a hunter;
when Brahman is united with Śakti, then it attains the state of a deity. || 18 ||
O Pārvatī, O Great Goddess, know that my own scripture is Prakṛti;
within my own scripture, all the Vedas and various Tantras are contained.
"Indeed, O Goddess, dear one, nothing exists apart from one's own scripture (svāgama).
Therefore, O Supreme Sovereign, everything is remembered as being composed of primordial nature (prakṛti). (20)
O Pārvatī, he who possesses scholarship [should always provide] the universe, consisting of ten million manifestations and endowed with all powers,
as well as its support.
O Goddess of pure smiles, whatever else there may be—such as muteness or poetic talent—all that, O Supreme Sovereign of pure smiles, one should know to be Śakti. (22)
O Supreme Goddess, O Beloved, Śakti is always the union of Brahmā; O Beloved, both Śabdabrahman and Parabrahman are always endowed with Śakti.
Thus, O Maheśānī, Brahman is praised as the Śabdabrahman;
and its cause, O Goddess, is Mātṛkā, whose form is Brahman. (24)
For this very reason, O Great Goddess, it has always resided within my heart;
yet, out of devotion to you, O lady of pure smiles, I have declared that which is indeed most secret.
One who desires his own welfare must not speak of this to anyone. (25)
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter in the venerable Bhūtaśuddhi-tantra, in the dialogue between Hara and Pārvatī. || 16 ||
Now begins the seventeenth chapter.
The venerable Lord said:
O Great Goddess, this Tantra [prevails] in heaven, on earth, and in the netherworld.
It shall always be praiseworthy, O Goddess; my word cannot be otherwise. || 1 ||
O Maheśānī, in whatever kingdom this Tantra exists, O Deveśī, there shall be no portents of calamity nor any fear at any time.
O Goddess, diseases would not destroy anyone anywhere in that kingdom;
nor was there fear of pestilence there, nor any disease at that time, O Beloved.
O Goddess, one obtains that fruit which belongs to all dharmas among all phenomena, and that fruit which belongs to all sacrifices, by worshipping this book. (4)
O Goddess, that house in which my rare book is found is as difficult to find on earth as Kāmarūpa itself. || 5 ||
O Great Goddess, in whose house this book is always present,
all the sacred fords, such as Kāśī and others, reside within his very home.
O Goddess with a lotus-like face, in whatever house this book exists, that house is always filled with all the gods; it is always filled with all the gods.
O Great Goddess, he in whose house this Tantra, which consists of all the Agamas, is always present—he indeed is such; it can never be otherwise.
O fair-faced one, he in whose house this tantra is always present is equal to all the scriptures; my word is not otherwise.
A Concise Exposition on the Purification of the Elements (Bhūtaśuddhi)

Having visualized a rampart of fire with the syllable *ram* and a stream of water, one should place both hands palm-upward on one's lap. Thinking "I am He," one should unite the individual soul (*jīvātman*)—residing in the heart in the form of a lamp-flame—with the *Kulakuṇḍalinī* residing at the *mūlādhāra*, via the path of the *suṣumṇā*. Having pierced the six chakras known as *mūlādhāra*, *svādhiṣṭhāna*, *maṇipūra*, *anāhata*, *viśuddha*, and *ājñā*, one should join it with the Supreme Self situated within the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus facing downward at the head. There, one should contemplate the dissolution of the twenty-four principles: earth, water, fire, air, ether; smell, taste, form, touch, sound; nose, tongue, eyes, skin, ears; speech, hands, feet, anus, genitals; and nature, mind, intellect, and ego. Then, contemplating the smoke-colored wind-seed *yam* at the left nostril, one should fill the body with air by reciting it sixteen times. Holding the nostrils, one performs *kumbhaka* (retention) by reciting it sixty-four times. One should dry up the body along with the black-colored "sin-man" (*pāpapuruṣa*) located in the left side of the abdomen, and exhale the air through the right nostril by reciting [the seed-syllable] thirty-two times. Next, meditating on the red-colored fire-seed *ram* at the right nostril, one fills the body with air by reciting it sixteen times. Holding the nostrils, one performs *kumbhaka* by reciting it sixty-four times. One should burn the body along with the sin-man by means of the fire rising from the *mūlādhāra*, and exhale through the left nostril by reciting it thirty-two times. Then, meditating on the white-colored moon-seed *ṭham* at the left nostril, one leads the moon to the forehead by reciting it sixteen times. Holding the nostrils, one constructs the entire body out of the nectar dripping from that moon on the forehead—consisting of the letters of the *Mātṛkā*—by reciting the water-seed *ram* sixty-four times. Finally, contemplating the body as very firm by reciting the earth-seed *lam* thirty-two times, one should exhale the air through the right nostril.
Thus ends the venerable Bhūtaśuddhi Tantra.
